usable.name: Analyzing marine biofilms developed on carbon nanotube-modified surfaces by 3D OCT approach (data for Polymers 2022, 14, 4410)
subjects: substrates: glass, epoxy resin, CNT composite
7 weeks, controlled hydrodynamics, 6 timepoints (7/14/21/28/42/49 d) x 3 surfaces, n=21 measurement rows
method: Optical Coherence Tomography (wet weight + OCT structure)
usable.reason: all of I1-I5 hold; CC-BY-4.0 stated in the record

spatial_frame.V7a_unit_and_datum: lengths in µm; the datum is the solid coupon surface (glass / epoxy / CNT composite). The deposit declares NO origin offset and NO axial direction: it is a scalar mean±SD per coupon, not a profile.
spatial_frame.V7b_geometry: the reported 'Biofilm thickness' is a FULL thickness of a laterally extended film, NOT a cluster radius and NOT a half-depth. Any use as a spherical cluster radius R would overstate the diffusion length by ~2x.
spatial_frame.V7c_volumetric: OCT-derived; the deposit does not publish voxel size, stack axis order or segmentation threshold -> those are UNKNOWN, so the porosity figure cannot be traced to a segmentation rule from the deposit alone.

usable.name: Supplemental Material for 'The EPS-I exopolysaccharide transforms Ralstonia wilt pathogen biofilms into viscoelastic fluids' (Rheometry data)
usable.format: zip of 83 CSV files (UTF-16LE) + 1 metadata xlsx
subjects: Ralstonia solanacearum: WT GMI1000 and epsB mutant, plus IBSBF1503, lecF, lecFX, lecX, nucAB, PSI07, XCC8004
scraped colony biofilms, parallel-plate oscillatory rheometry: flow curve / amplitude sweep / frequency sweep
usable.reason: I1-I5 hold and license is explicit (MIT), but the deposit publishes no tau_y column and the crossover extraction was NOT DONE in the time budget -> tau_y from S3 = UNKNOWN

spatial_frame.V7a_unit_and_datum: rheometer sample = a scraped colony biofilm, not an in-situ film; no spatial datum applies (rheology is a bulk measurement).
spatial_frame.V7b_geometry: N/A for a bulk modulus, but this is exactly why it does NOT transfer directly to Q160's tau_y: a G'/G'' crossover from a ~1 Hz-10 rad/s oscillatory sweep is strain-rate dependent and frequency dependent, whereas Q160's tau_y is a static yield stress of a porous matrix under bulk flow shear. Different measured quantity, same symbol.

usable.name: same record, Moisture content measurement repeat
subjects: Ralstonia WT GMI1000 n=8 and epsB mutant n=8
gravimetric wet/dry mass of scraped colony biofilm
usable.reason: gives moisture 90.07-90.64 %w/w, but a MASS fraction; no dry-matrix density is given, so it cannot be converted to a porosity without an assumption -> conversion UNKNOWN

spatial_frame.V7a_unit_and_datum: gravimetric bulk sample; no spatial datum. This is a MASS fraction, not a volume fraction -> converting to a porosity requires an assumed bulk density of the dry matrix, which the deposit does not give. UNKNOWN.

usable.name: Radial profiles of growing microbial colonies through interferometry
subjects: 9 strains (bgt127, bh1514, cc117, ea387, gob33, jt305, sw519, sw520, y55)
colonies from a 1.5 µL OD600=1 droplet on LB agar (bacteria) or YPD (fungi), 23.8 °C
Zygo ZeGage Pro optical profilometer, 2729 measurement rows, t = 0.21-336.8 h, replicates per strain
constrains: T5 cluster/colony geometry (with the caveat below)
usable.reason: CC0, all files small, geometry is measured with an explicit datum

spatial_frame.V7a_unit_and_datum: heights in µm, and the README states the media background was SUBTRACTED, so z = 0 is the AGAR SURFACE. Heights are therefore FULL colony heights above the substrate, not depths into a slab and not radii.
spatial_frame.V7b_geometry: the deposit is a RADIAL PROFILE of a hemispherical-ish colony grown from a 1.5 µL droplet. mid_height is a height (vertical), NOT a cluster radius. Using mid_height as Q160's spherical cluster radius R would be a CATEGORY ERROR: Q160's t90_cluster() assumes isotropic radial diffusion into a sphere of radius R.
spatial_frame.V7c_volumetric: Zygo ZeGage Pro optical profilometer, 1000x200@800Hz mode; profiles stitched in x then averaged over ~32 µm in y. xy pixel size is not stated in the deposit -> UNKNOWN.

usable.name: PIV vector fields from: Boundary layer hydrodynamics of patchy biofilms
usable.size: 9018 bytes downloaded; the 4 PIV zips are 6.0-6.2 GB each
subjects: 4 non-uniform diatomaceous biofilms (PB-1, PB-2, SB-1, SB-2) on large acrylic plates
water 23.3-23.7 °C, 4000 instantaneous velocity fields per biofilm
constrains: T7 tau_b (CALIBRATION ONLY - no shear values deposited at the reachable size)
usable.reason: the 9 kB metadata file passes I1-I5 but contains only temperature and px/inch calibration; it does NOT numerically constrain tau_b = 0.5 Pa

spatial_frame.V7a_unit_and_datum: calibration is px/inch -> 11.9-13.1 µm per pixel at these magnifications.
spatial_frame.V7b_geometry: PIV over a flat plate; the velocity field is a boundary-layer field ABOVE the biofilm, not a field inside it. Cannot be used as an internal pore velocity.
